note: The closest thing in this batch to the ICP as stated. Owns a commercial cleaning and pressure-washing company with employees, started at 19, building to sell within three years. Income is evidenced rather than claimed — he quotes his own jobs at 2,000 to 15,000 and treated the 6,000 as arithmetic, not an obstacle. Health is the neglected corner of an otherwise ordered life, not a crisis: he trains consistently, walks 20,000 steps in season and does multi-day fasts. Good-to-great is explicit — self-rated 5-6 out of 10 and asking to be taken to 9-10. Not deconditioned by any reading. The one criterion the stated ICP does not contain is the one that matters here: four disclosed joint complaints including pain specifically on overhead pressing, in a programme built on loaded overhead kettlebell work. That is the clinical gap already noted in icp.json, appearing again in a prospect who otherwise scores clean on all five stated criteria.
